steps.title: Syrah only
steps.body: Syrah is the only red grape allowed in the northern Rhône. It gives deep, peppery wines with blackberry, violet, olive and smoked meat. Some appellations let small amounts of white grapes be co-fermented with it: up to 20% Viognier in Côte-Rôtie, 15% Marsanne and Roussanne in Hermitage, though most use much less.

steps.title: White grapes
steps.body: Viognier makes Condrieu and Château-Grillet: rich, apricot and violet. Marsanne and Roussanne make white Hermitage, Crozes-Hermitage, Saint-Joseph and Saint-Péray, where they also make sparkling wine. Marsanne gives body; Roussanne gives aroma and freshness.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its main use.
steps.explanation: The northern Rhône has a short grape list.

steps.body: Co-fermenting a little Viognier with Syrah helps fix colour and adds a floral lift. In Côte-Rôtie, it's typically 2 to 5%.

steps.prompt: Which is the only red grape allowed in the northern Rhône?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Syrah is the northern Rhône's only red grape
Viognier makes Condrieu; Marsanne and Roussanne white Hermitage
Small amounts of white grapes can be co-fermented with Syrah
